text: Ukraine's General Staff says it struck the Marinovka airfield in Russia's Volgograd region overnight on November 26.
Kyiv says Su-34 fighter-bombers are based there.

The General Staff also claims a hit on the Subkhankulovo oil pumping station in Bashkortostan, more than one thousand kilometres from the Ukrainian border, and says a tank was damaged and a fire broke out.
Local authorities in the Tuymazy district reported a fire in an industrial zone after a drone attack, without naming the facility.
Deutsche Welle, citing Astra and Ukrainian monitoring channels, reports drone debris also hit the Nevinnomyssk power plant in Stavropol territory.
At least thirty-one people have been killed and twenty-one injured after a fuel tanker crashed and caught fire on a ring road in Cairo, according to Egypt's health ministry.
The Guardian reports the blaze happened on Wednesday evening in the Warraq area of Giza, a densely populated neighbourhood.
Al-Ahram, citing people familiar with the investigation, says the tanker driver lost control after a high-voltage cable fell in front of the vehicle.
The public prosecutor has opened an investigation and ordered DNA samples taken from the dead.
The health ministry says the death toll is preliminary.
The ring road has since reopened.
US regulators have approved a plan by SpaceX to launch a million satellites into orbit to build data centres in space, according to the BBC.
The Federal Communications Commission says the project, called Starmind, will support America's artificial intelligence economy.
The satellites would be powered by sunlight and process data for AI systems before sending results back to Earth.
Under the licence, deployment must begin by November 2033.
Amazon has criticised the plan as a lofty ambition, and US astronomers warn it could significantly affect night-sky observation.
Dw Glavnoe also reports that the first satellites are planned for late 2027.
Ukraine has received the bodies of 250 soldiers from Russia, while Russia received 22 bodies in return, according to the BelTA news agency in Belarus.
Ukrainian media outlet UNIAN and DW also report the exchange.
The Ukrainian ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, said Russia handed over 250 bodies that Moscow claims belong to Ukrainian servicemen.
Identification will be carried out by Ukrainian investigators.
The BBC Russian Service reports that some previously repatriated remains did not match Russia's descriptions.
The exchange followed the resumption of trilateral talks mediated by the United States.
The United States has proposed new tariffs on fourteen of its key trading partners, according to Al Jazeera and the BBC.
The partners include China, the European Union, India, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.
China faces the highest rate, up to 40 percent.
Vietnam faces up to 35 percent, and the others face rates of 20 or 25 percent.
The US Trade Representative announced the proposals on Wednesday, citing unfair trade practices that harm American manufacturing.
The BBC reports the duties are not expected to take effect until next year, and must first go through public consultation and possibly hearings.
The BBC reports that Iranian women sentenced to death over the January protests are appealing for help.
According to the BBC's Persian service, twenty-one-year-old Taraneh Rahimi has been unable to walk properly in recent weeks after her legs were beaten.
Her cousin, Masoud Nourmohammadi, says an untreated head injury led to an ear infection that has affected her balance.
He says she signed a confession after interrogators threatened to rape her sister in front of her.
UN human rights rapporteur Mai Sato says Rahimi is one of six women sentenced to death this year over the protests.
The Iranian embassy in London called claims of rising protest-related death sentences misleading and rejected allegations of torture.
A deputy commander of Russia's Aerospace Forces, Yuri Grekhov, has been arrested in Moscow.
According to the Kommersant newspaper, a record of the arrest appeared in the database of the 235th garrison military court in Moscow.
The court made the decision on November 25.
The official reason for the arrest has not been announced.
Sources told Kommersant that Grekhov is accused of taking a bribe on a particularly large scale.
Grekhov holds the rank of colonel general.
BBC Russian also reported the arrest, citing Kommersant.
Myanmar says it will not comply with parts of a United Nations court ruling on genocide against the Rohingya.
According to the BBC, President Min Aung Hlaing made the statement at a meeting on Wednesday, saying the country would not follow requirements it considers inappropriate.
He did not say which parts of the ruling he meant.
Last week, the International Court of Justice found Myanmar guilty of genocide over a 2017 military crackdown in Rakhine State.
The court ruled by nine votes to six.
Myanmar denies the charge.
The court's ruling is final, but the court has no direct means to enforce it.
